title: Add and reset two score variables
careers: Software testers check that counters and displays reset cleanly before a new user starts.
goal: I can create two named score variables in my maze project and set both to zero on start.

slides.title: Add and reset two score variables
lines: I can create two clear score variables.
I can set both variables to zero on start.
I can place both readouts clearly on the stage.
I can save and check my maze project.
slides.cue: Choose one variable skill to practise today.
slides.notes: Introduce the Autumn 2 continuation of the two-level maze project for the unit award. All variable names and rules come from supplied made-up project cards A and B. Keep personal names, places and external account details out of the task.

slides.title: Our maze skills from last half-term
lines: Where does your player sprite start?
How does your start script reset the maze?
Where do you save your project file?
Choose made-up project card A or B today.
slides.cue: Show or explain how your maze resets on start.
slides.notes: Retrieve the Autumn 1 maze routine: agreed folder, useful file name, start-position reset, save, close and reopen check. If a pupil's Autumn 1 maze file is absent, open the clean two-level starter maze file from the practice folder.

slides.title: Which start script is fair?
lines: Look at Project A and Project B. Which start script gives a fair fresh start?
slides.cue: Choose a project and explain why it is fair.
slides.notes: Compare a start script that leaves old scores untouched with one that resets both score variables to zero on start. Explain that initialising variables on start gives every player a fair turn.
answers: Project B is fair because both score variables reset to zero when the start event runs.
Without a reset block, old points stay on screen from the last turn.

slides.title: Clear names for two variables
lines: Give each score variable a name that matches its job.
Create one variable for pickups and one for hazards.
slides.cue: Point to the two variable names on the model.
slides.notes: Demonstrate making two variables in the block editor using Card A: FuelScore and HazardHits. Show how clear names tell anyone reading the script what each number tracks. Avoid vague names such as number1 or var.

slides.title: Reset both variables on start
lines: Place two set-to-zero blocks directly under the start event.
Keep the variable readouts away from the maze walls.
slides.cue: Point to the two blocks that reset the scores.
slides.notes: Model attaching set FuelScore to 0 and set HazardHits to 0 directly under the start hat block on the player sprite. Drag the two stage readouts to the top corners so the start pad and maze walls stay visible.

slides.title: Words for score variables
lines: variable: a named store for a value that can change
initialise: set a starting value when the project begins
reset: return a value to zero for a fresh start
readout: the box on stage that shows a variable value
slides.cue: Explain one word using the model script.
slides.notes: Teach the four terms with the model script and stage view. Connect initialise and reset to the two set-to-zero blocks under the start event.

slides.title: Match each block to its job
lines: Set FuelScore to 0. Set HazardHits to 0.
Show FuelScore at top left. Show HazardHits at top right.
slides.cue: Match each pair of rules to its setup step.
slides.notes: Use Space maze card A. The two set-to-zero blocks belong under Start reset. The two readout positions belong under Stage display. Allow pointing or sorting printed cards before building the script.
answers: Start reset: set FuelScore to 0; set HazardHits to 0.
Stage display: show FuelScore at top left; show HazardHits at top right.

slides.title: A partner tests the start reset
lines: Change one variable to 5, then trigger start. Does it return to 0?
Can the player see the start zone and both readouts clearly?
slides.cue: Give one useful fix after the reset test.
slides.notes: Model a deliberate test: temporarily set a variable to 5, trigger the start event, and verify that both readouts return to 0. Check that neither readout covers the start zone or finish target.
answers: Both readouts must return to 0 every time the start event runs.
Move a readout box if it covers the start zone or a maze wall.

slides.title: Add two score variables to your maze
lines: Supported: use the variable name and reset frame.
Independent: create and reset both score variables.
Aspire: add a round counter that starts at one.
Each person saves and checks their own project file.
slides.cue: Choose a route and set up your variables.
slides.notes: Slides 10-13 share this 12-minute task time. Each pupil updates their own maze file. A shared device uses six-minute turns: Card A then Card B, with builder and tester roles. Keep the focus on naming and resetting two variables.

slides.title: Supported
lines: Choose made-up project card A or card B.
Create the two named variables on your card.
Attach two set-to-zero blocks to the start event.
Place both readouts at the top with help.
Save, reopen and test the start reset.
slides.cue: Show your two variables and their zero values.
slides.notes: Use the editable route page as a planning frame. Provide one step at a time or exact scribing for variable names, then record that support. The pupil selects the blocks and runs the start reset test.

slides.title: Independent
lines: Choose project card A or B and create both variables.
Attach both set-to-zero blocks to the start script.
Place both stage readouts clear of the maze path.
Test the reset by setting a test number and restarting.
Save your file, then reopen it to check.
slides.cue: Ask your partner to test your start reset.
slides.notes: The pupil uses the chosen project card to create and initialise both variables on the player sprite. Save in the agreed Week 1 folder under Maze_Score_A_v1 or Maze_Score_B_v1 with the software's native extension.

slides.title: Aspire
lines: Complete the Independent task first.
Add the third variable from your card for the round count.
Set the round variable to 1 under the start event.
Ask a partner to test all three readouts on start.
Save a new version and explain one change.
slides.cue: Show how all three variables initialise on start.
slides.notes: Use the card's stretch rule to add RoundCount (Card A) or DiveCount (Card B) initialised to 1 on start. Save a separate v2 copy and retain v1. Explain why a round counter starts at 1 while scores start at 0.

slides.title: My evidence record
lines: My file name is ...
My pickup variable is ...
My hazard variable is ...
I changed ... because ...
I reopened the saved file and tested the reset.
slides.cue: Record your own variable names and the help used.
slides.notes: Observe two named variables, two set-to-zero blocks attached to start, clear readout placement and reopen result. Record actual prompts or scribing. One next-step prompt is followed by the pupil's response and an adult acknowledgement. Do not prefill pupil codes or success boxes.

slides.title: How do we know the start is fair?
lines: Show your two variables and your start reset blocks.
Explain why both scores must reset to zero on start.
Open your saved file and run the start check.
slides.cue: Show your project and give one reason.
slides.notes: Three minutes for individual checks, two for feedback and close. Check the saved file, not just the open draft. Week 2 updates scores from two maze events. Week 7 is the assessing lesson; this week is formative.

steps: Choose card A or B. Read the two variable names.
Make one pickup variable and one hazard variable.
Attach two set-to-zero blocks under the start event.
Test the reset to zero. Save and reopen your file.
words: A named store for a value that can change.
Set a starting value when the project begins.
Return a value to zero for a fresh start.
The box on stage that shows a variable value.
A trigger that starts a script running.
Run the project to check that a rule works.
